study type: Ecological study (cross-sectional survey and registry data analysis)
exposure: Organizational characteristics of maternity units (e.g., continuous on-site presence of gynecologist/anesthetist, operating room location, transfer time, unit size, presence of NICU)
Number of cesarean sections performed in the maternity unit
outcome: Proposal rate of Trial of Labor After Cesarean (TOLAC)
Success rate of Trial of Labor After Cesarean (TOLAC)/Vaginal Birth After Cesarean (VBAC)
cohort: The study analyzed data from 95 Belgian maternity units.
finding: Organizational characteristics of maternity units, particularly continuous on-site staff and the overall unit cesarean section rate, significantly influence the proposal and success rates of trial of labor after cesarean section.
mod_finding: Continuous on-site presence of a gynecologist and an anesthetist was associated with a higher proportion of TOLAC proposal, while a higher overall number of cesarean sections in a unit negatively correlated with both TOLAC proposal and success.
cross-section timing: N/A (data collected around the study publication year for organizational factors and from regional perinatal registries, no specific single time point or range mentioned for the registry data itself)
